title: Tricky Sam Nanton portrait
summary: Nanton was naturally funny, loved by all, with a West Indian-inflected growl that told stories; Brown thinks no one captured his gift.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: We have mentioned Tricky Sam every so briefly, just that he was there with the trombone section. I know he was a very important voice and force in the band. Tell me about Tricky Sam.

Well, he was a man that had many talents, and most of his talents were -- he was unconscious of. His playing was one talent, and he had a natural gift for being funny. You'd just look at Tricky Sam and his big eyes -- and he was funny. And his music backed up his being funny because his music was funny too. He was a very nice fellow. We got along very well. He -- with everybody -- everybody loved Tricky Sam. And as I say, he and Bubber Miley were the basis of the band in its early days.

And he had a way of phrasing his music that was -- I don't think anyone has ever picked up on that. And it's just lost because no one even tried to catch the true meaning of his music. His parents were from the West Indies, and that West Indian influence was kept in his playing. And everything he you played, you could tell that was Tricky Sam because with the growel, it was almost like talking.

His -- you take some of his early records and it's really like telling a story. And the sad ways that he could make his horn sound was really something. I don't think anybody has ever tried to really capture his gift.
Did he ever live in the West Indies?

No, he lived in New York. He was a New Yorker, but his parents were from the West Indies. And they have odd cadences and odd accents and odd things that fit perfectly in this jungle type band that Ellington had.
Did he have that kind of cadence in his speech too?
No, he had a very -- he had a high voice and big eyes, and when you'd see him he was just comical -- just naturally comical. And as I say, everybody loved him.
